newsitem.title: UK: LME copper at $2,500 in late London.
newsitem.headline: LME copper at $2,500 in late London.

text.p: London Metal Exchange (LME) three months copper was indicated at around $2,500 per tonne, its strongest for a year, in late London inter-office trading.

Last kerb business had been at $2,493, up $19 on the day, after a bounce from negative territory, then in after-hours trading it steamed higher. It was bid at $2,500 by the time Comex closed at 1800 GMT.
Investment funds, commission houses, banks and the trade covering shorts were all said to have contributed to a burst of buying that swept the market higher in the last minutes of the kerb.
"This is an excellent close for copper at fresh highs and it bodes extremely well for tomorrow," said analyst William Adams of broker Rudolf Wolff.
"I think people were convinced they had seen the bottom," said Robin Bahr at Brandeis.
Players may also have been anticipating a decision by the U.S. monetary authorities to leave interest rates unchanged. A brisk U.S. economy would be good for metals sector, Bahr said.
News at around 1815 GMT that the FOMC had indeed left rates unchanged did not, however, prompt any immediate fresh move up by copper.
But any stocks draw on Wednesday of several thousand tonnes might further buoy the market.
